extracted.intended_audience: State and Federal Exchange officials, issuers, agents/brokers/web-brokers, navigators/CACs, consumer advocates, and other stakeholders invited to comment on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: A federal proposed rule regarding the timing and administration of Open Enrollment Periods (OEPs) and Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs) on Health Insurance Exchanges, plus program-integrity and verification changes. The page explains proposed regulatory text changes, empirical justifications, and solicits public comment and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance OEP extension benefits vs risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether an extended Open Enrollment Period (OEP) provides a balanced approach to provide consumers additional time to make informed choices and increase access to health coverage, while mitigating risks of adverse selection, consumer confusion, and issuer and Exchange operational burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider State Exchange experience with January extensions, evidence that only a small number of consumers used the extra time to switch plans, and tradeoffs between added enrollment opportunity and potential adverse selection, consumer confusion, and administrative burdens. Provide data on enrollment changes, plan switching, and operational impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt December 15 OEP end date nationwide
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the OEP end date from January 15 to December 15 for the coverage year (proposed to apply to all Exchanges for the 2026 coverage year and beyond).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification includes reducing consumer confusion over two deadlines, decreasing inadvertent dual enrollment and coverage start-date casework, and reducing burdens on Exchanges and issuers. Note potential Federal/State/issuer outreach costs to alert consumers of the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider delaying effective date due to PY2026 subsidy changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Request comment on whether to delay the effective date for the proposal to update the OEP end date until the OEP preceding PY 2027, given special circumstances for PY 2026 financial assistance (expiration of ARP/IRA enhanced subsidies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for likely plan cost increases when enhanced subsidies expire and the potential for increased demand for additional time to choose plans for PY 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit Exchanges from extending OEP via blanket SEP
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek comment on whether the Secretary should prohibit Exchanges from extending an OEP through application of a blanket special enrollment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should include data demonstrating the impact of OEP end dates and extensions on enrollment and adverse selection. Consider potential operational difficulties for State Exchanges and whether State-level transitional SEPs are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove the 150 percent FPL SEP
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to repeal the monthly SEP for APTC-eligible qualified individuals with projected household income at or below 150 percent of the FPL (§155.420(d)(16)) and conforming regulatory changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale includes increased improper enrollments facilitated by access to fully subsidized plans, incentives to wait until sick to enroll (adverse selection), and evidence (complaints, enrollment–population disparities) that the SEP has been abused. Also note statutory interpretation that the SEP is not authorized by the listed SEP statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align SEP availability with statutory SEP list
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that Exchanges provide only the SEPs authorized by statute (sections 1311(c)(6)(C) and (D) of the ACA and section 9801 of the Code) and that any additional SEPs are similar in circumstances to Medicare Part D SEPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argue that the 150 percent FPL SEP is dissimilar to Part D SEPs and not among SEPs in section 9801; solicit comments on this legal interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigate improper enrollments by agents/brokers/web-brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Address and reduce improper enrollments and unauthorized plan switching conducted by some agents, brokers, and web-brokers (including enrolling consumers without knowledge, changing agent of record, switching plans to capture commissions, splitting households).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use system and logic changes, enforcement, outreach, and program integrity measures; cite consumer complaint trends (e.g., December 2024 complaints vs prior periods) and litigation. Solicit information on mechanisms exploited and additional remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstate and expand pre-enrollment SEP verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §155.420(g) to reinstate (with modifications) pre-enrollment verification of eligibility for SEPs on the Federal platform and require all Exchanges to conduct pre-enrollment verification for at least 75 percent of new enrollments through SEPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: verification protects the risk pool and program integrity by deterring ineligible mid-year enrollments. Provide operational experience from prior years (response times, resolution rates) and consider impacts on enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh verification tradeoffs for risk pool vs deterrence
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider that verification protects the risk pool from ineligible individuals enrolling only when they are sick, but verification can deter eligible enrollees (especially younger/healthier individuals) and thus could harm the risk pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical data (PY2017–PY2019 experience, SVI resolution rates, percent unable to resolve) to evaluate whether verification's positive impact on the risk pool exceeds negative effects from deterring enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empirical metrics to detect improper enrollments and adverse selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and quantify improper enrollments and adverse selection using complaint counts, comparisons of plan selections to Census population estimates by income band, enrollment growth among APTC-only enrollees, and percent of enrollees dropping coverage between key dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from analysis: fewer than 3% of enrollees ended coverage between Dec 15 and Jan 15 (470,000 individuals); large complaint spikes (e.g., 7,134 improper-enrollment complaints December 2024); comparisons showing plan selections exceeding Census population estimates (e.g., Florida data implying >1 million improper enrollments). Solicit state-level experiences and datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate premium and Federal cost impacts of SEP/OEP policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Project how SEPs and OEP timing affect premiums and Federal Premium Tax Credit (PTC) costs (e.g., earlier projection that 150% FPL SEP would increase premiums by 3–4%; updated projection 0.5–3.6% after accounting for waiting-to-enroll behavior and improper enrollments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for both legitimate adverse selection impacts and mitigating effects of improper enrollments (people unknowingly enrolled may not file claims). Consider downstream Federal subsidy costs when evaluating SEP policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider consumer outreach and administrative costs of changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for the costs to the Federal government, State Exchanges, and issuers if additional outreach is needed to alert consumers to changes in the OEP end date or SEP rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List potential outreach channels (Mail notices, advertising campaigns, assistor collaboration, HealthCare.gov hub) and include considerations of timing, messaging, and operational burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit comments on OEP duration and calendar placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Request public comment on overall effects and impacts of OEP duration and placement within the calendar year, including suggestions regarding the ideal duration and placement to minimize adverse selection and maximize consumer choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage commenters to provide data and suggestions about ideal duration/placement to balance enrollment access and market stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require commenters to provide state-specific data on improper enrollments
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage commenters and interested parties to share experiences in their States, including the extent of improper enrollments and other data disparities (e.g., enrollment vs population mismatches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use state-level analyses to corroborate national findings (e.g., comparisons showing disproportionately high plan selections in certain income bands in multiple States).
